facts.fact_text: The opposition planned to hold a demonstration on 12 January 2013 in Baku.
The opposition planned to hold a demonstration on 26 January 2013 in Baku.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 12 January 2013.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 26 January 2013.
Shortly after the demonstration of 12 January 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse the assembly.
Shortly after the demonstration of 26 January 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse the assembly.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation of the demonstration of 12 January 2013.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation of the demonstration of 26 January 2013.
No prior notice was given to the Baku City Executive Authority by the organisers of the demonstration planned for 12 January 2013.
No prior notice was given to the Baku City Executive Authority by the organisers of the demonstration planned for 26 January 2013.
The Baku City Executive Authority was the relevant authority to receive prior notice of demonstrations.
At the time of both of the applicant's arrests, under Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.

Before the amendments introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, which entered into force on 1 January 2013, any breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies was punishable under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 by a reprimand or a fine of AZN 7 to 13.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 entered into force on 1 January 2013.
Both of the applicant's arrests occurred after the amendments introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 were enacted.

At the time of the applicant's arrests, Article 298.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that any breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies, demonstrations, protests, marches and pickets by an organiser of an assembly who is an individual shall be punished by a fine of AZN 1,500 to 3,000; or, depending on the circumstances of the case and the personality of the perpetrator of the offence, by community service for 200 to 240 hours or administrative detention for up to 15 days.
At the time of the applicant's arrests, Article 298.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that a person in charge shall be punished by a fine of AZN 3,000 to 6,000.
At the time of the applicant's arrests, Article 298.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that a legal entity shall be punished by a fine of AZN 15,000 to 30,000.

At the time of the applicant's arrests, Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that participation in an assembly, a demonstration, a protest, a march or a picket which was not organised in accordance with the rules set forth under the legislation shall be punishable by a fine of AZN 300 to 600; or, depending on the circumstances of the case and the personality of the perpetrator of the offence, by community service for 160 to 200 hours or administrative detention for up to 15 days.

The Note to Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that if there are elements of a crime in actions proscribed under Articles 298.1 and 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences, the perpetrator of those actions bears criminal responsibility under the relevant Articles of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan.
Shortly after the demonstration of 12 January 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse the assembly.
Shortly after the demonstration of 26 January 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse the assembly.
In the first case, the Nasimi District Court sentenced the applicant to a fine of 500 Azerbaijani manats (AZN).
In the second case, the Nasimi District Court sentenced the applicant to a fine of AZN 400.
According to the applicant, the hearing before the Nasimi District Court in the first case was very brief.
According to the applicant, the hearing before the Nasimi District Court in the second case was very brief.
